chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Zurarah, from Isa ibn Abd Allah al-Hashimi, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali عليه السلام, who said:
The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: When you enter the place of relieving yourself, do not face the qiblah and do not turn your back to it, but rather turn eastward or westward.
And with this chain, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abi al-Ala' or someone else, raising it, who said:
Al-Hasan ibn Ali عليه السلام was asked: What is the limit regarding defecation? He said: Do not face the qiblah, do not turn your back to it, do not face the wind, and do not turn your back to it.
As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who said:

I entered upon Abi al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام, and in his house there was a lavatory facing the qiblah. This report does not contradict the first two reports, because it contains no more than that he saw a lavatory that had been built in this manner, and he did not mention that he saw him sitting on it, or that he permitted that, or ordered it to be built in this manner. It is also possible that the house had been transferred to him while it had already been built that way; if the matter was like that, then sitting on it would be permissible.

key_terms.الْإِسْنَادِ: the chain of narrators transmitting the report
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةَ: the direction of the Ka'bah used for worship

ai.seo_question: What do the hadith say about facing the qiblah while using the lavatory?
ai.summary: This report concerns the fiqh ruling and etiquette of relieving oneself in relation to the qiblah. It transmits prohibitions against facing or turning one’s back to the qiblah, and also mentions not facing or turning one’s back to the wind, while reconciling another report about a lavatory built toward the qiblah.
